title: Two-way power: PNB, bidirectional devices and sources
oneLine: A4 is now the only edition; PNB is a recognised TN-C-S variant with its own box on the forms; A3's rule says each protective device must suit the direction power flows; and a battery is a generating set, connected on the supply side of the final circuit devices, never on the load side of an RCD where 551.7.1(d) forbids it.
skill: Recognise and record a PNB supply; tell a unidirectional device from a bidirectional one and spot one being back-fed; place a battery or other source correctly in a board; know the dates and that editions are not mixed.
specRefs: No syllabus: an update course to BS 7671:2018+A4:2026 for an A2-trained designer and inspector (brief section 1)
materialRefs: a4-pocket-guide.txt section 3.0 (PNB, 312.2.1.1) and 6.0 (batteries as generating sets, bidirectional flow, sources on the load side of an RCD)

to research: SELECT 'So what's new' (PNB, Figure 3.9B, ESQCR 8(4), definitions); Hager bitesize guide (551.7.1 (c) and (d), device markings); IET A4 forms (TN-C-S (PME) and (PNB) boxes); the A4 book for 551.7.1(d)'s conditions
picture: A board fed by the grid, PV and a battery. A switch flips import to export and arrows show the current's direction through each device; a unidirectional RCBO fed from its load side turns red, a bidirectional one stays green. A second control moves the battery's connection: supply side of the final circuit devices (green), onto a final circuit like a load (red, 551.7.2.1), or on the load side of an RCD (flagged, 551.7.1(d)). Directions only, no invented currents.
builds_on: Design and verification lesson 6 (TN-C-S supplies, Ze)
Design and verification lesson 7 (protective devices and breaking capacity)

title: Boards and batteries: what can overload an assembly
oneLine: A board and its RCCBs are protected against overload by one of three routes: the feeding device no bigger than their ratings, load curtailment, or the whole connected load within them; diversity is never one of them. A parallel generator adds 551.7.2.2's four options, and Chapter 57 sets where a battery goes, its RCD type and its notices.
skill: Check a board's InA and an RCCB's Inc against the feeding device, the connected load and any load management; apply 551.7.2.2 where PV or a battery runs in parallel; check a battery installation's location, ventilation, RCD type, isolation and notices.
specRefs: No syllabus: an update course to BS 7671:2018+A4:2026 for an A2-trained designer and inspector (brief section 1)
materialRefs: a4-pocket-guide.txt section 5.0 (536.4.202, load curtailment) and 6.0 (Chapter 57, PAS 63100)

to research: Hager bitesize guide (the three 536.4.202 routes, InA and Inc, the four 551.7.2.2 options, the notice; 570.6.2.2 Type B unless; 570.6.8.201 and .203 notices); SELECT (diversity not load curtailment, load control or overload protection; Chapter 57 scope and exclusions); IET FAQ and EVC webinar Q&A (A2's 536.4.202, 536.4.3.2)
picture: A board with an example InA of 100 A. Drag the incoming device through 60, 80, 100 and 125 A, add circuits from a palette, and switch on diversity, load management or PV export. Three route lamps show which of 536.4.202's routes holds; diversity changes the demand figure but never lights a lamp. With PV on, a 551.7.2.2 panel works InA against each of its four options. Every sum is computed from the shown rule.
builds_on: Design and verification lesson 2 (maximum demand and diversity)

title: Fire, walls and wiring
oneLine: AFDDs are required in high-rise residential buildings, not every Building Safety Act 'higher-risk' building; escape routes gain rules for fire-fighting shafts, protected stairways and fire-resisting enclosures; concealed cables follow one table by wall type and depth; buried cables need armour or an N750 duct; and RCDs in series must each suit the residual current they may see.
skill: Decide what a concealed or buried cable run needs; apply the escape route and premature collapse rules for what they are; identify functional earth conductors; terminate fine-wire conductors properly; choose RCD types and selectivity in series; know when a firefighter's switch is needed.
specRefs: No syllabus: an update course to BS 7671:2018+A4:2026 for an A2-trained designer and inspector (brief section 1)
materialRefs: to research: SELECT (422.2.201, 422.2.202, the 522.6 table, the N750 note, Table 51 pink, conductor classes, 537.4.2); Hager (421.1.7's reason, 531.3.3 note, 536.4.1.4 note, Figure 534.5); the A4 book for the table and escape route numbering
picture: A wall elevation with a socket and a switch. Drag a cable route and the 150 mm zones shade in; toggles for depth under or over 50 mm, metal parts in the wall, and a 30 mA RCD. A panel says what the run needs: zone and RCD, the 522.6.204 protection, or nothing more. A 'bury it' toggle moves the run outdoors, where it needs earthed armour or an N750 duct.
builds_on: Design and verification lesson 3 (selecting the cable)

title: New and changed installations: PoE, ICT earthing, EV, outdoor lighting, medical, marinas
oneLine: Power over Ethernet is now in BS 7671: a compliant source of not more than 60 V DC dry or 15 V elsewhere, and not more than 750 mA a conductor; ICT gets its own functional earthing section; EV points may use an RDC-PD and need no AFDD; public lighting needs a 30 mA RCD; medical locations are rewritten; and marinas isolate the hull from shore earth.
skill: Check a PoE run's source and current per conductor; recognise ICT functional earthing and bonding; choose an EV point's RCD or RDC-PD; apply 714's RCD rule and its notes; know the medical location and marina changes an inspector meets.
specRefs: No syllabus: an update course to BS 7671:2018+A4:2026 for an A2-trained designer and inspector (brief section 1)
materialRefs: to research: SELECT (716.414.1.1 sources, cable categories; 714 scope; 709.313.1.101; 702.55.5; 710 detail; 722.421.1.7.201); Hager (714.411.3.4 notes); BEAMA A4 presentation (RDC-PD); IET press release (750 mA per contact); a maker's IEEE 802.3 note for real PoE voltages and pair counts
picture: A PoE run. Drag the power at the port, choose two or four pairs and the source voltage; the current per conductor, P ÷ V shared over the conductors carrying each polarity, is computed against a 750 mA line. The source voltage turns red over 60 V, or over 15 V with 'wet location' ticked. No invented temperatures.
builds_on: Design and verification lesson 6 (the EV Section B answer)

title: Inspection, testing and the EICR
oneLine: The tests do not change; the EICR does. Section K splits into C1 and C2, which make a report unsatisfactory, and C3 and FI, which are advisory; FI is 'advised' and only for what the inspection's limits hid; the report follows the rewritten notes, carries guidance for the recipient, may include photographs, and is signed by those who did the work. The forms add PNB and a few notes.
skill: Code observations and reach the right outcome under A4; use FI only where it belongs; read an A3 report correctly; complete the A4 EIC, minor works and EICR, including PNB and Zdb; know what in Chapter 64 did not change.
specRefs: No syllabus: an update course to BS 7671:2018+A4:2026 for an A2-trained designer and inspector (brief section 1)
materialRefs: to research: IET A4 EIC, minor works and EICR forms (Section K's two parts, the outcome note, PNB, Zdb, AFDD and SPD notes, the maximum Zs source note); IET Wiring Matters 110 'Further investigation' (history, the two misuse examples); NICEIC A4 page; SELECT (653.1, 653.2, photographs); Wiring Matters 102 (signatures)
picture: An EICR's Section K with eight example observation cards, each labelled as an example. Drag each into part one or part two and code it; a switch flips between A3 and A4 rules and the overall outcome changes on the FI cards only. Two cards are traps, an unlabelled circuit and a 0.6 MΩ reading: put either in FI and the card says why it needs a code instead.
builds_on: Design and verification lesson 9 (verification and handover)
